key_insight: FDE-Gym shifts AI evaluation from clean, predefined benchmarks to messy, real-world delivery work where requirements are ambiguous and constraints emerge during execution. It provides a realistic testbed for measuring how well agents handle the “last mile” of deployment and customer delivery.
problem_solved: Most agent benchmarks focus on well-specified tasks with clear instructions, but real forward-deployed engineering involves ambiguous goals, live systems, and hidden constraints. This paper addresses the gap between benchmark performance and the practical challenges of customer-facing AI delivery.
method: Built FDE-Gym as a benchmark of 95 end-to-end delivery tasks drawn from 20 customer scenarios across 18 industries.
Tasks were adapted from real-world delivery projects by industry experts to preserve realism and complexity.
The benchmark simulates the interactive, uncertain conditions FDEs face when clarifying requirements and operating in live environments.
impact: FDE-Gym gives AI researchers and practitioners a more realistic way to evaluate agents for deployment-oriented work. It can help reveal whether models are truly ready for customer-facing delivery, not just narrow benchmark tasks.

paper_title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
paper_authors: Dongxu Yang, Hongda Yan, Renxin Wang, Baoli Zhang, Haojia Zuo
